concepts.name: Meaning and features of religion
concepts.description: Definitions of religion from different angles (belief in the sacred or supernatural, a way of life, a community of believers), the common features of religions (beliefs, rituals and worship, sacred places, objects and times, sacred texts or oral traditions, practitioners, moral codes, symbols, community) and the dimensions of religion in outline (Ninian Smart's seven dimensions named only as one scholar's model). Key terms: sacred and profane, faith, worship, ritual, myth, symbol. Theories of origin are frs.religion.origins-theories.

concepts.name: Theories of the origin of religion
concepts.description: Explanations of how religion began, presented as theories to compare, not facts: revelation (religions' own accounts), animism (E. B. Tylor), totemism and the social theory (Émile Durkheim), the psychological theory (Sigmund Freud), Marx's view of religion in society, and the fear/wonder at nature explanation; strengths and criticisms of each in outline. Types of belief (monotheism, polytheism, pantheism, atheism, agnosticism) are frs.religion.study-approaches.

concepts.name: Functions of religion for individuals and society
concepts.description: Roles of religion for the individual (meaning, identity, comfort, moral guidance), the family, the community and the nation (social cohesion, social control, welfare, education, health, rites of passage, legitimising authority, social change), and its possible negative effects (conflict, exploitation, fundamentalism, harmful practices) presented in a balanced way. Detailed contemporary issues (education, gender, health, conflict) are in topics 7-15.

concepts.name: Religious diversity and tolerance in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: The religions practised in Zimbabwe (Indigenous Religion, Christianity in its many denominations, Islam, Judaism, and smaller communities such as Hinduism and the Bahá'í faith in outline), religious pluralism, freedom of conscience and religion in the Constitution of Zimbabwe 2013 (section 60), religious tolerance, interfaith dialogue and cooperation, and the multi-faith, non-confessional approach of this subject. No population percentages unless taken from a cited census or survey and labelled with its year.

concepts.name: Key concepts for studying religion
concepts.description: Types of belief about the divine (monotheism, polytheism, henotheism, pantheism, atheism, agnosticism, secularism), revelation (general and special), the insider and outsider (emic/etic) perspectives, the phenomenological, comparative and multi-faith approaches, and why the subject is non-proselytising and non-confessional (describe and understand beliefs without judging or converting). Definitions of religion are frs.religion.meaning-features.

concepts.name: Religion, morality and Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu
concepts.description: Meaning of morality, ethics, values and norms; sources of morality (religion, culture, conscience, law, reason); the relationship between religion and morality; the philosophy of Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu (being human through others: respect, sharing, hospitality, responsibility, humility) and how Indigenous Religion, Judaism, Christianity and Islam each support these values. Applied ethics (health, sexuality, bioethics) is topic 9 (frs.ethics.*).

concepts.name: Nature and sources of Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Meaning and features of Indigenous Religion (IR): no single founder or written scripture, transmitted orally, integrated with daily life, community-based; its sources (myths, legends, proverbs, songs, prayers, rituals, sacred places, art, names and totems, elders' oral traditions); misconceptions and loaded labels (paganism, heathenism, 'ancestor worship') discussed fairly with the view of many scholars that ancestors are venerated as intermediaries. God and spirits in detail are separate concepts.

concepts.name: The concept of God and creation in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Names of God in Zimbabwean IR (Mwari, Musikavanhu, Nyadenga, Dzivaguru, Chikara in Shona; uMlimo, uNkulunkulu, uSimakade in Ndebele; other groups' names where certain) and what they express; attributes of God (creator, provider, rain-giver, transcendent yet active); God's relationship with ancestors and people; creation myths and myths of the origin of death presented as traditional narratives; the Mwari cult at the Matopo shrines (Njelele/Matonjeni) in outline.

concepts.name: The spirit world in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Categories of spirits as believed in IR: family ancestral spirits (midzimu/amadlozi), territorial or tribal guardian spirits (mhondoro/ amadlozi of the land, e.g. Nehanda, Chaminuka, Kaguvi as figures of history and belief), alien spirits (mashavi), avenging spirits (ngozi) and the belief in witchcraft (uroyi/ubuthakathi) and its social consequences; how spirits are believed to communicate and act. Presented descriptively; no endorsement or ridicule; accusations of witchcraft and their harm handled carefully. Spirit mediums and healers as practitioners are frs.indigenous.practitioners.

concepts.name: Religious practitioners in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Roles of IR practitioners and leaders: spirit mediums (masvikiro), traditional healers and herbalists (n'anga/inyanga; the herbalist (inyanga) and diviner (isangoma) distinction in Ndebele usage), diviners, rain-makers, chiefs and headmen as custodians of tradition and land, family elders and aunts and uncles (vatete, sekuru) in family rituals, the Zimbabwe National Traditional Healers Association (ZINATHA) in outline. No claims that traditional medicine cures disease.

concepts.name: Sacred places, objects, attire and symbols in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Sacred places (mountains, caves, pools, forests and groves, shrines such as Njelele in the Matopo Hills, Great Zimbabwe as a religious and national site, graves), sacred objects (snuff, beer pots, ritual axes, staffs, drums, mbira), religious attire and colours (black, white and red cloths of spirit mediums, beads, animal skins), totems as sacred symbols in outline (identity aspects are frs.family.names-totems), taboos protecting sacred places. Rituals performed there are frs.indigenous.worship-rituals.

concepts.name: Worship, rituals and sacred days in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Forms of worship and rituals: prayer through ancestors, offerings and libations (doro/umqombothi, snuff), the bira/ukuthetha ceremony, rain-making (mukwerera/ukucela izulu), thanksgiving and first-fruits ceremonies, the role of music, dance, clapping and the mbira and drums, sacred days of rest (chisi/ the rest day observed in a chiefdom) and their significance. Rites of passage (birth, initiation, marriage, death) are separate concepts.

concepts.name: Birth, naming and initiation rites in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Rites of passage defined (separation, transition, incorporation, after van Gennep in outline); pregnancy and birth customs (care of the mother, the birth hut, the umbilical cord and fontanelle customs in outline), naming and its meaning, introduction of the child to the family and ancestors; initiation and puberty rites among groups that practise them (e.g. Venda vhusha and domba, and the initiation schools of some Tsonga/Shangani and Remba (Lemba) communities) described factually and respectfully, their purpose (adulthood, sex education, values) and contemporary debates (health, consent, schooling). Marriage and death rites are separate concepts.

concepts.name: Marriage in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Meaning and purpose of marriage in IR (union of families, procreation, continuity of lineage, involving ancestors); the marriage process (courtship, go-between (munyai/umkhongi), bride wealth (roora/lobola) and its parts in outline, the role of aunts and uncles, the ceremonies of welcoming the bride); types of marriage (monogamy, polygamy, levirate/inheritance of a widow, sororate, pledging and kuzvarira, elopement) with their advantages and the harmful practices now illegal (child and forced marriage; the Marriages Act 2022 sets 18 as the minimum age). Christian, Jewish and Muslim marriage are in their religions' rites concepts.

concepts.name: Death, burial and the afterlife in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Beliefs about death (causes as understood in IR, death as a transition to the spirit world), funeral and burial rites (preparing the body, the role of relatives, the grave, mourning customs, purification), the bringing-home ceremony (kurova guva/umbuyiso) about a year later and why it matters, inheritance rituals in outline, the living dead and the role of ancestors in the life of the family; changes due to urbanisation and other religions.

concepts.name: Moral teachings, taboos and sanctions in Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Sources and content of IR morality (respect for elders, hospitality, honesty, sharing, chastity, respect for nature), taboos (zviera/imilayo) and their purposes (social order, health, conservation, respect) with examples, proverbs and folk tales as moral teaching, rewards and sanctions (social, ancestral and supernatural, fines by chiefs' courts), and the relevance of IR morality today. The general link between religion and morality is frs.religion.morality-unhu.

concepts.name: Indigenous Religion in contemporary Zimbabwe
concepts.description: How IR has met Christianity, colonialism, urbanisation, education and technology; responses (decline, continuity, adaptation, revival); syncretism and the African Independent/Initiated Churches as one meeting point (detail in frs.christianity.zimbabwe); the legal and constitutional recognition of traditional institutions and healers in outline; how IR still shapes identity, ceremonies and national life. Balanced: no claims that IR is dying or that it is superior.

concepts.name: Origins of Judaism: the patriarchs and the covenant
concepts.description: Meaning of Judaism and the names Hebrews, Israelites, Jews; the call of Abraham and the covenant (Genesis 12, 15, 17), circumcision as the sign of the covenant, Isaac and the binding of Isaac (Genesis 22), Jacob renamed Israel and the twelve tribes, Joseph in Egypt (Genesis 37-50) in outline; the matriarchs (Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Leah). Narratives presented as the Jewish scriptures tell them; dating of the patriarchal period is uncertain (no precise dates).

concepts.name: Moses, the Exodus and the covenant at Sinai
concepts.description: Slavery in Egypt, the call of Moses (Exodus 3), the plagues and the first Passover (Exodus 12), the crossing of the sea, the covenant at Sinai and the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20; Deuteronomy 5), the tabernacle and the ark, the wilderness years and the entry into Canaan under Joshua in outline; why the Exodus is central to Jewish identity. The Passover festival today is frs.judaism.sabbath-festivals; the commandments as ethics are frs.judaism.ethics.

concepts.name: From kingdom to diaspora: the history of Judaism
concepts.description: The judges, the monarchy (Saul, David, Solomon and the First Temple), the divided kingdom (Israel and Judah) and the prophets in outline, the Babylonian exile (586 BCE) and return, the Second Temple and its destruction by the Romans (70 CE), the rise of rabbinic Judaism and the diaspora; in outline the persecution of Jews in Europe, the Holocaust (about six million Jews murdered), and the establishment of the State of Israel (1948); Jewish communities in Zimbabwe (Harare and Bulawayo synagogues) and the Lemba (Remba) tradition of Jewish ancestry presented as a claim studied by scholars. No position on current Middle East politics.

concepts.name: Jewish beliefs
concepts.description: Belief in one God (the Shema, Deuteronomy 6:4-9, paraphrased), God as creator, just and merciful, the covenant and the idea of a chosen people (with its meaning of responsibility), the Torah as God's teaching, the Messiah (mashiach) as awaited, beliefs about the afterlife (olam ha-ba, resurrection) as varied among Jews, Maimonides' Thirteen Principles of Faith in outline. Scriptures are frs.judaism.scriptures.

concepts.name: Jewish scriptures: Tanakh and Talmud
concepts.description: The Tanakh and its three parts (Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim), the Torah scroll (Sefer Torah) and how it is treated, the oral Torah, Mishnah and Talmud, the role of rabbis' commentary; how Jews use scripture in worship and daily life; the relationship with the Christian Old Testament in outline. Quoting: cite book, chapter and verse and paraphrase.

concepts.name: Jewish worship, the synagogue and religious leaders
concepts.description: The synagogue (features: ark, Torah scrolls, bimah, ner tamid, separate seating in Orthodox synagogues), daily prayer and the minyan, the rabbi, cantor (hazzan) and historical priests (kohanim) and Levites, religious attire and symbols (kippah, tallit, tefillin, the Star of David, the menorah), worship in the home. Sabbath and festivals are frs.judaism.sabbath-festivals.

concepts.name: The Sabbath and Jewish festivals
concepts.description: Shabbat (from Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall: rest from work, candles, kiddush, family meal, synagogue, havdalah) and its basis (Genesis 2; Exodus 20); the pilgrim festivals Pesach (Passover, the seder), Shavuot and Sukkot; the High Holy Days Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur; Hanukkah and Purim in outline; how festivals are observed and what they mean. Rites of passage are frs.judaism.rites-passage.

concepts.name: Jewish rites of passage
concepts.description: Birth and brit milah (circumcision on the eighth day) and naming, bar mitzvah (13) and bat mitzvah (12 or 13), marriage (betrothal, the ketubah, the chuppah, breaking the glass) and divorce (the get) in outline, death, burial and mourning (shiva, kaddish, the yahrzeit). Meaning of each rite and differences among Jewish groups.

concepts.name: The Jewish home and food laws
concepts.description: The home as a centre of religious life (mezuzah, Shabbat and festival meals, teaching children), the dietary laws (kashrut: kosher and treif, permitted animals, separation of meat and milk, kosher slaughter (shechitah)) and their scriptural basis (Leviticus 11; Deuteronomy 14) in outline, and reasons Jews give for observing them; family roles. Ethical teaching is frs.judaism.ethics.

concepts.name: Groups within Judaism
concepts.description: Main movements: Orthodox (including Haredi and Hasidic), Conservative/Masorti, Reform/Progressive/Liberal, and secular Jews; Ashkenazi and Sephardi traditions; how they differ on Torah, worship, the role of women and dietary practice, presented without ranking. The history of the diaspora is frs.judaism.kingdom-diaspora.

concepts.name: Jewish moral teaching
concepts.description: The Ten Commandments as moral law, the 613 mitzvot in outline, justice (tzedek), charity (tzedakah), loving-kindness (gemilut hasadim), love of neighbour and the stranger (Leviticus 19:18, 34), the sanctity of life (pikuach nefesh), repairing the world (tikkun olam), care for the poor, family and sexual ethics in outline, and the prophets' call for justice (e.g. Amos 5; Micah 6:8) paraphrased.

concepts.name: The life of Jesus
concepts.description: Background (Palestine under Roman rule, Jewish groups: Pharisees, Sadducees, Zealots, Essenes), the birth narratives (Matthew 1-2; Luke 1-2), baptism and temptations, the call of the disciples, the ministry in Galilee, miracles in outline, the entry into Jerusalem, the Last Supper, arrest, trial, crucifixion, resurrection and ascension as the Gospels record them; Jesus in the Jewish setting. Teachings are frs.christianity.teachings-jesus. Presented as what the Gospels say and Christians believe.

concepts.name: The teachings of Jesus
concepts.description: The Kingdom of God, the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7: Beatitudes, the law fulfilled, prayer and the Lord's Prayer, the Golden Rule), selected parables (the Good Samaritan, the Prodigal Son, the Sower, the Lost Sheep) and their meanings, love of God and neighbour (Mark 12:28-34), forgiveness, care for the poor and outcasts, and their relevance today. Cite and paraphrase; no long quotations.

concepts.name: The early Church and the spread of Christianity
concepts.description: Pentecost (Acts 2), the apostles Peter and Paul, Paul's conversion and missionary journeys in outline, the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15), persecution under Rome, the Emperor Constantine (Edict of Milan 313) and the Council of Nicaea (325), the spread of Christianity into North Africa and Ethiopia (early African Christianity: Alexandria, Carthage, the Ethiopian church). Divisions are frs.christianity.denominations.

concepts.name: Christian denominations
concepts.description: The Great Schism of 1054 (Orthodox and Catholic), the Reformation from 1517 (Martin Luther, John Calvin, the Church of England) and the Protestant churches, Methodists and Baptists in outline, the Pentecostal movement (twentieth century), African Independent/Initiated Churches; main differences in authority, sacraments, worship and leadership presented without ranking; ecumenism (World Council of Churches, Zimbabwe Council of Churches, Zimbabwe Catholic Bishops' Conference, Evangelical Fellowship of Zimbabwe) in outline.

concepts.name: Christianity in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Early Portuguese Catholic contact (Gonçalo da Silveira at the Mutapa court, 1561), the London Missionary Society at Inyati (1859), later missions (Jesuits, Methodists, Anglicans, Dutch Reformed, Salvation Army, Seventh-day Adventists, Brethren in Christ) and their links with colonisation, mission education and health, African Independent/Apostolic churches (e.g. Johane Masowe, Johane Marange, the Zion Christian Church) and Pentecostal churches (e.g. the Apostolic Faith Mission, ZAOGA) in outline, and Christianity's place in Zimbabwe today. Churches in the liberation struggle are frs.liberation.churches.

concepts.name: Christian beliefs
concepts.description: God as creator, the Trinity (Father, Son and Holy Spirit), the incarnation, sin and salvation, grace and faith, the atonement, the resurrection, the Holy Spirit and the Church, life after death (heaven, hell, judgement, purgatory in Catholic belief), the second coming; the creeds (Apostles' and Nicene) in outline; how denominations differ on some beliefs.

concepts.name: The Bible
concepts.description: Structure (Old Testament and New Testament, the main book groups), the canon and the Apocrypha/Deuterocanonical books in outline, inspiration and interpretation (literal and non-literal readings), translation (the Bible in Shona and Ndebele) and how Christians use the Bible in worship, study and daily life. Cite and paraphrase; no long quotations.

concepts.name: Christian worship, leaders and places of worship
concepts.description: Forms of worship (liturgical and non-liturgical, charismatic, the Sunday service, prayer, preaching, hymns and choruses), places of worship (church buildings and their features, open-air sites and sacred shrines used by apostolic churches), practitioners and leaders (pope, bishop, priest, pastor, deacon, elder, evangelist, prophet in AICs), attire and symbols (cross and crucifix, vestments, the white garments of apostolic churches, the dove, the fish). Sacraments are frs.christianity.sacraments-rites.

concepts.name: Sacraments and rites of passage in Christianity
concepts.description: Meaning of sacrament; baptism (infant and believers' baptism), the Eucharist/Holy Communion/Lord's Supper, confirmation, marriage, ordination, reconciliation (confession), anointing of the sick; denominational differences (seven sacraments in Catholic and Orthodox churches, two ordinances in most Protestant churches); Christian rites of passage at birth, marriage and death (funeral, burial, memorial and tombstone unveiling).

concepts.name: Christian festivals and sacred days
concepts.description: Sunday as the Lord's Day (and the Saturday Sabbath of Seventh-day Adventists), the Christian year: Advent and Christmas, Epiphany, Lent and Ash Wednesday, Holy Week (Palm Sunday, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday), Easter, Ascension, Pentecost; their meanings and how they are observed in Zimbabwe (e.g. Easter gatherings of apostolic churches, Christmas).

concepts.name: Christian moral teaching
concepts.description: Sources (the Bible, the teaching of Jesus, the Church, conscience), the Ten Commandments, love (agape) and the Golden Rule, forgiveness and reconciliation, justice and care for the poor, stewardship, honesty and work, sexual and family ethics in outline, and Christian social teaching and service. Application to specific issues is in topics 6-15.

concepts.name: Pre-Islamic Arabia and the life of the Prophet Muhammad
concepts.description: Arabia before Islam (Makkah, the Ka'bah, tribal society, the Jahiliyyah as Muslims describe it), the life of the Prophet Muhammad (born about 570 CE in Makkah, first revelation about 610 CE in the cave of Hira, preaching and opposition in Makkah, the Hijrah to Madinah in 622 CE (start of the Islamic calendar), the community in Madinah, the return to Makkah in 630 CE, death in 632 CE); Khadijah and the early Muslims. Presented as Muslim tradition relates it; the Prophet is not depicted in any image.

concepts.name: The caliphs and the spread of Islam
concepts.description: The four rightly guided caliphs (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali), the origin of the Sunni and Shi'a division, the spread of Islam into North and West Africa and along the East African coast through trade, the Swahili coast and Arab-Swahili traders in the Zimbabwe plateau trade (Sofala) in outline, and Islam in Zimbabwe today (communities of Malawian, Mozambican and South Asian origin and Zimbabwean converts; mosques in Harare, Bulawayo and other towns). Groups within Islam are frs.islam.groups-sharia.

concepts.name: Muslim beliefs: the articles of faith
concepts.description: Tawhid (the oneness of God, Allah) and shirk, the angels (e.g. Jibril), the revealed books (Tawrat, Zabur, Injil, Qur'an), the prophets and messengers (Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad as the seal of the prophets), the Day of Judgement and the afterlife (paradise and hell), and divine decree (al-Qadr); the meaning of Islam and Muslim. Shi'a additional beliefs are frs.islam.groups-sharia.

concepts.name: The Qur'an, Hadith and Sunnah
concepts.description: The Qur'an as revealed to Muhammad through Jibril over about 23 years, its compilation (under Abu Bakr and the standard text under Uthman), structure (114 surahs, ayat, Makkan and Madinan surahs, Al-Fatihah), recitation and memorisation (hafiz) and respect for the text; the Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet) and Sunnah, the major collections (Bukhari, Muslim) in outline, and their use. Cite surah and ayah and paraphrase.

concepts.name: The Five Pillars: Shahadah and Salah
concepts.description: The Five Pillars introduced; the Shahadah (declaration of faith) and its meaning; Salah: the five daily prayers and their times, wudu (ablution), the qiblah towards the Ka'bah, the adhan, the rak'ah and postures in outline, prayer mats, Jumu'ah (Friday congregational prayer); the significance of prayer. Zakat, Sawm and Hajj are frs.islam.pillars-zakat-sawm-hajj.

concepts.name: The Five Pillars: Zakat, Sawm and Hajj
concepts.description: Zakat (obligatory giving, usually 2.5% of qualifying wealth held for a year, its recipients) and voluntary charity (sadaqah); Sawm (fasting in Ramadan from dawn to sunset, who is exempt, its purposes, Laylat al-Qadr); Hajj (pilgrimage to Makkah in Dhul-Hijjah for those able: ihram, the Ka'bah, tawaf, sa'i, Arafat, Mina and the stoning, the sacrifice) and its meaning; Umrah in outline. The Eid festivals are frs.islam.mosque-festivals.

concepts.name: The mosque, leaders and Muslim festivals
concepts.description: The mosque (masjid) and its features (prayer hall, mihrab, minbar, minaret, ablution area, no images), its roles in the community and madrasah education, leaders and practitioners (imam, muezzin, scholars (ulama), qadi), dress and modesty (hijab, kufi) presented as practice varies; the Islamic (lunar) calendar; festivals and sacred days (Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Mawlid an-Nabi observed by many Muslims, Islamic New Year, Ashura) and how they are celebrated.

concepts.name: Rites of passage in Islam
concepts.description: Birth (the adhan whispered to the newborn, tahnik, aqiqah and naming on the seventh day, shaving the head), circumcision of boys, marriage (nikah: consent, mahr, witnesses, walimah; polygyny of up to four wives under conditions in outline; divorce (talaq) in outline), death (washing, shrouding, the funeral prayer, prompt burial facing Makkah, mourning). Meaning of each rite.

concepts.name: Islamic law, ethics and groups within Islam
concepts.description: Sharia and its sources (Qur'an, Sunnah, consensus (ijma), analogy (qiyas)) and the schools of law in outline; halal and haram (food, alcohol, interest (riba), dress), moral teachings (justice, honesty, charity, family, respect for parents); the correct meaning of jihad (greater: inner struggle; lesser: defence under strict conditions) and the rejection of terrorism by mainstream Muslim scholars; Sunni and Shi'a Islam (beliefs about leadership, the imams) and Sufism, presented without ranking.

concepts.name: The concept and structure of the family
concepts.description: Form 1. Meaning of family, types (nuclear, extended, single-parent, child-headed, blended, polygamous), roles and relationships of members, kinship terms (e.g. vatete/ubabakazi, sekuru/umalume, babamukuru) and the importance of belonging to a family; family as understood in Indigenous Religion, Judaism, Christianity and Islam in outline. Changing family forms are frs.family.changing-family.

concepts.name: Indigenous Religion and family identity
concepts.description: Form 1. How IR shapes family identity: ancestors as members of the family, family rituals, the roles of elders, aunts and uncles in passing on identity, the home and the homestead, inheritance of names and roles, respect and obligations within the family. Totems and names are frs.family.names-totems; IR rites in detail are frs.indigenous.*.

concepts.name: Names, totems and identity
concepts.description: Form 2. Meaning and significance of names in IR, Judaism, Christianity and Islam (naming customs and the meanings of names), totems (mutupo/isibongo) and praise poetry (detembo/izibongo) in outline, their roles (identity, preventing incest, conservation, unity), and the effect of change (Christian and Muslim names, urban life). Totems as sacred symbols are taught here from the identity angle.

concepts.name: Family values, community values and Indigenous Religion
concepts.description: Form 2. Family values (respect, love, obedience, sharing, hard work, honesty, chastity) and community values (cooperation, hospitality, nhimbe/ilima work parties, collective responsibility for children, care for the vulnerable), IR and the community (the chief, the village, shared rituals), and how Judaism, Christianity and Islam support the same values. Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu itself is frs.religion.morality-unhu.

concepts.name: Inter-dependency of families
concepts.description: Form 3. How families depend on one another (marriage alliances, kinship networks, mutual help at funerals, weddings, harvest and in illness, community child care, burial societies and savings clubs), the role of religion in building these links (church, mosque and synagogue communities, IR ceremonies), and threats to inter-dependency (individualism, migration, conflict).

concepts.name: Religion, Zimbabwean identity and African identity
concepts.description: Forms 3 and 4. How Indigenous Religion contributes to Zimbabwean identity (heritage sites, national ceremonies, language, values, national heroes linked to IR) and to African identity (shared beliefs, Ubuntu, Pan-African cultural revival), how other religions in Zimbabwe have been Africanised (African Independent Churches, Islam in Africa), and debates about identity in a multi-faith nation. Heritage-only detail (national symbols) belongs to Heritage Studies, not here.

concepts.name: Changing culture, types of families and national values
concepts.description: Form 4. How culture and the family are changing (urbanisation, migration and the diaspora, education, technology and social media, economic pressure, HIV and AIDS, child-headed and single-parent families, cohabitation), religious responses to these changes, the family and national values (Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu, patriotism, hard work, respect for human rights), and ways of strengthening families. Marriage law in outline only.

concepts.name: Indigenous education and religion
concepts.description: Education in traditional society: aims, content (skills, values, history, religion), methods (observation, participation, folk tales, proverbs, songs, initiation, the dare/ixhiba for boys and the kitchen for girls in outline), teachers (parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, the community) and its strengths and limitations; the religious content of indigenous education. Mission and modern schooling are frs.education.institutions.

concepts.name: Religion and the establishment of educational institutions
concepts.description: The role of religious organisations in founding schools, colleges, hospitals' training schools and universities in Zimbabwe (mission schools from the nineteenth century such as Inyati, Hope Fountain, Chishawasha, Old Mutare, Kutama, Waddilove, Dadaya in outline; church universities such as Africa University (United Methodist, Mutare), the Catholic University of Zimbabwe, Solusi University (Adventist)), Islamic madrasah and Muslim schools, Jewish schools in outline; the contribution to human-resource capacity and the link to colonial policy. Only institutions whose founding church is certain are named.

concepts.name: The role of religion in education and nation building
concepts.description: How religious bodies support education today (running and supporting schools, teacher training, scholarships, special-needs education, values and moral education, chaplaincy), partnership with government as responsible authorities, contribution to national development and human resource, and criticisms (cost, denominational bias, proselytising concerns) presented fairly.

concepts.name: Negative impacts of religion on education
concepts.description: Religious beliefs and practices that can keep children from formal education or limit it (e.g. some groups' refusal of schooling or of particular subjects, child marriage and pledging, gender bias against educating girls, conflict between scientific and religious views), the constitutional right to education (section 75) and the Education Amendment Act 2020 in outline (free and compulsory basic education as policy), and how communities and religious leaders address these problems. No group named unless the fact is well documented, and then without stigma.

concepts.name: Gender, gender roles and stereotypes
concepts.description: Meaning of sex and gender, gender roles, gender stereotypes, gender equality and equity, patriarchy, gender-based violence (GBV); how roles are learned (socialisation by family, religion, school, media); gender in the Constitution of Zimbabwe (section 17 gender balance, section 56 equality) in outline. Religious teachings on gender are frs.gender.ir-judaism and frs.gender.christianity-islam.

concepts.name: Gender roles in Indigenous Religion and Judaism
concepts.description: Roles of men and women in IR (women as spirit mediums, healers, aunts (vatete) with ritual authority; men as family heads; division of labour; lobola and inheritance customs and their effects on women) and in Judaism (creation accounts in Genesis 1-2, women of the Hebrew Bible such as Sarah, Miriam, Deborah, Ruth, Esther; roles in Orthodox and Progressive Judaism, women rabbis in Reform Judaism), described fairly and with evidence.

concepts.name: Gender roles in Christianity and Islam
concepts.description: Christian teaching and practice on gender (Genesis 1:27; Galatians 3:28; Ephesians 5 and differing interpretations; women in the ministry of Jesus; women's ordination accepted in some denominations and not in others; women's church groups such as Ruwadzano and Manyano in outline) and Muslim teaching and practice (equality before God, Qur'an 4:1, rights of women in marriage, inheritance and property, dress and modesty, women scholars such as Aisha; different interpretations among Muslims); described fairly without ranking religions.

concepts.name: Religion, gender equality and gender-based violence
concepts.description: How religions can promote or hinder gender equality today, religious responses to gender-based violence and harmful practices (child marriage, virginity testing, wife inheritance, denial of inheritance), women in religious leadership, men's roles as partners in equality, and the law in outline (Constitution, Domestic Violence Act 2007, Marriages Act 2022). Balanced, with the view that each religion contains resources for dignity and justice.

concepts.name: Religion, health and healing
concepts.description: Religious understandings of illness and healing (IR: physical, spiritual and social causes; traditional healers; Christianity: healing ministry of Jesus, prayer, anointing, faith healing in AICs and Pentecostal churches, mission hospitals; Islam: health as a trust, prophetic medicine in outline; Judaism: saving life comes first), cooperation and conflict with modern medicine (e.g. refusal of treatment or vaccination by some groups, children's right to health care); safe, factual health information only.

concepts.name: Religion and sexuality
concepts.description: Meaning of sexuality and responsible sexual behaviour, religious teachings on sex and marriage (chastity before marriage, faithfulness in marriage, the purpose of sex) in IR, Judaism, Christianity and Islam, teenage pregnancy, sexual abuse and exploitation (and where to report: Childline Zimbabwe 116), and the age of consent in outline (raised to 18 after the Constitutional Court ruling of 2022 and later legislation; writers check the current law and state only what is certain). Age-appropriate, non-graphic; diverse religious views on sexual orientation stated factually without endorsing hostility.

concepts.name: Religion and HIV and AIDS
concepts.description: Basic facts (HIV and AIDS, transmission routes, prevention, testing, antiretroviral therapy), stigma and discrimination and religious teaching against them, religious responses (care for the sick and orphans, home-based care, prevention messages: abstinence, faithfulness, condoms where religions differ, testing before marriage), harmful beliefs (that prayer replaces treatment) handled carefully. Accurate, non-stigmatising health information only.

concepts.name: Religion and drug and substance abuse
concepts.description: Meaning and types of drugs and substances (alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, crystal meth (mutoriro), cough syrups such as bronclee, inhalants), causes and effects on individuals, families and society, religious teachings (IR uses of beer in ritual and taboos against drunkenness, Christian teaching on drunkenness, Islam's prohibition of intoxicants, Jewish teaching on moderation), and religious and community responses (prevention, rehabilitation).

concepts.name: Religion and life issues: abortion, euthanasia and medical ethics
concepts.description: The sanctity and quality of life, religious views on abortion (with the Termination of Pregnancy Act in outline), contraception and family planning, infertility treatment (IVF, surrogacy), euthanasia, organ donation and blood transfusion, and the death penalty in outline, showing the range of views within and between IR, Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Balanced, factual, no persuasion.

concepts.name: Moral decision-making and contemporary moral issues
concepts.description: How people make moral decisions (scripture, religious authority, conscience, reason, consequences, situation ethics, Unhu), and religious perspectives on contemporary issues not covered elsewhere: corruption, honesty and theft, gambling and get-rich-quick schemes, violence and bullying, social media ethics. Applied ethics on health, sexuality and life issues are separate concepts.

concepts.name: Disability: meaning, types and causes
concepts.description: Meaning of disability and impairment, the medical and social models of disability in outline, types (physical, visual, hearing, intellectual, albinism as a condition often discussed with disability, mental health conditions, multiple) and causes (genetic, disease, accidents, malnutrition, conflict), and myths and misconceptions about the causes (witchcraft, punishment, curses) explained and corrected respectfully. Respectful language (person-first).

concepts.name: Religious teachings and attitudes towards disability
concepts.description: Teachings and attitudes in IR (beliefs about causes, care within the extended family, harmful practices historically), Judaism (Leviticus 19:14), Christianity (Jesus' healing ministry, John 9:1-3, care for the weak) and Islam (equality before God, Surah 80 ('Abasa) and the blind man, duties of care), and how attitudes can both support and stigmatise people with disabilities.

concepts.name: Religion, inclusion and the rights of people with disabilities
concepts.description: Rights of persons with disabilities (Constitution section 22 and 83, the Disabled Persons Act, the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities) in outline, inclusive education and inclusive worship (access, sign language, Braille), the role of religious organisations (special schools and centres, e.g. mission schools for the blind and deaf), and what individuals can do. Only institutions whose founding body is certain are named.

concepts.name: Religious teachings on the natural environment
concepts.description: Creation and humanity's place in it: IR (the land belongs to the ancestors and God; nature as sacred), Judaism and Christianity (Genesis 1-2: dominion understood as stewardship; Psalm 24:1; the Sabbath year for the land, Leviticus 25), Islam (humans as khalifah (vicegerent), the earth as a trust (amanah), Qur'an 6:165 and 30:41 paraphrased); comparison of the views.

concepts.name: Indigenous Religion and environmental conservation
concepts.description: How IR protects the environment: sacred forests, groves, mountains and pools, taboos (e.g. on cutting certain trees, on fishing in sacred pools), totems and the protection of animals, sacred days of rest for the land (chisi), the role of chiefs, spirit mediums and rain-making; effectiveness and decline of these methods; their use in modern conservation (CAMPFIRE in outline only).

concepts.name: Environmental problems and religious responses
concepts.description: Environmental problems in Zimbabwe and the world (deforestation, land degradation, veld fires, gold panning and river siltation, pollution and waste, poaching, climate change and drought), their causes, and responses by religious groups (tree planting, clean-up campaigns, teaching on stewardship, interfaith environmental work such as the Association of Zimbabwean Traditional Ecologists (AZTREC) and the Association of African Earthkeeping Churches (AAEC) in outline), with the law (EMA) in outline.

concepts.name: Religious teachings on work, wealth and poverty
concepts.description: The value of work and hard work (IR: nhimbe/ilima and laziness condemned; Judaism and Christianity: Genesis 2:15, Proverbs 6:6-11, 2 Thessalonians 3:10; Islam: honest earning), attitudes to wealth and poverty (stewardship, sharing, tithing, zakat and tzedakah), dangers of greed (1 Timothy 6:10), and the prosperity gospel debate presented fairly.

concepts.name: Religious organisations and enterprise
concepts.description: Enterprise and income-generating projects run by religious organisations (farms, schools, hospitals, publishing, transport, microfinance, skills centres, Islamic and church-based savings and welfare schemes), how they serve members and communities, entrepreneurship among believers (self-reliance, burial societies, savings clubs (mukando/round)), and problems (mismanagement, exploitation of followers, commercialisation of religion). Teachings on wealth are frs.enterprise.work-wealth.

concepts.name: Religion and business ethics
concepts.description: Religious teaching on honest trade (just weights, Leviticus 19:35-36; Qur'an 83:1-3 paraphrased), fair wages and workers' rights, lending and interest (usury in the Bible, riba in Islam and Islamic finance principles in outline), corruption and bribery, consumer protection, care for the environment in business, and the social responsibility of businesses and entrepreneurs.

concepts.name: Indigenous Religion in the First Chimurenga/Umvukela
concepts.description: The role of IR in the risings of 1896-97: the Mwari shrines and the Mwari priest Mkwati, the spirit mediums Kaguvi (Gumboreshumba) and Nehanda (Charwe Nyakasikana) in Mashonaland, the religious grievances and beliefs that inspired resistance, their capture and execution (Nehanda and Kaguvi executed in April 1898), and why historians debate how far the risings were coordinated by religious leaders. History detail belongs to history-o; here the religious dimension.

concepts.name: Indigenous Religion in the Second Chimurenga/Umvukela
concepts.description: How spirit mediums and IR supported the guerrilla war in the 1970s (spirit mediums in the north-east, e.g. the elderly Nehanda medium who went with ZANLA into Mozambique in the early 1970s, taboos observed by guerrillas, ancestral legitimacy, songs (chimurenga music) and night gatherings (pungwe) in outline), the relationship between fighters and rural communities, and different views of the role of IR. Factual and balanced; no graphic violence.

concepts.name: Christianity, Islam and the liberation struggle
concepts.description: Mixed roles of the churches: missionary links with colonial rule, mission-educated nationalist leaders, churches and church leaders who opposed settler rule (e.g. the Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace documenting abuses; Bishop Abel Muzorewa (United Methodist) and Rev. Ndabaningi Sithole as clergy in politics; Rev. Canaan Banana, a Methodist minister and later the first President) and those who supported the government; mission stations as places of refuge and conflict; the involvement of Muslims in outline only if documented; the World Council of Churches' Programme to Combat Racism grants in outline.

concepts.name: Religion, reconciliation and healing after the struggle
concepts.description: The policy of reconciliation at independence (1980), the role of religious organisations in reconciliation, healing and resettlement of ex-combatants and refugees, cleansing and reburial rituals in IR for the war dead, the national healing and reconciliation efforts (the Unity Accord 1987 and the National Peace and Reconciliation Commission (Constitution section 251) in outline), and the churches' role in later national dialogue. Non-partisan wording; no praise or blame of living politicians.

concepts.name: Religion and human rights
concepts.description: Meaning and characteristics of human rights, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) and the Declaration of Rights in the Constitution of Zimbabwe (Chapter 4) in outline, freedom of religion and its limits, religious foundations of human dignity (IR Unhu; humans in the image of God in Judaism and Christianity, Genesis 1:27; Islam on human dignity, Qur'an 17:70), and cases where religious practices and rights conflict (e.g. child marriage, denial of medical care), presented fairly.

concepts.name: Children's rights and responsibilities
concepts.description: Children's rights (Constitution section 81, the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child in outline: survival, development, protection, participation), children's responsibilities to family, school, community and religion, religious teachings on children (e.g. Exodus 20:12; Ephesians 6:1-4; Qur'an 17:23-24 paraphrased; IR teaching on respect), child abuse and protection, and reporting channels (Childline 116, police Victim Friendly Unit).

concepts.name: Religion and social responsibility
concepts.description: Meaning of social responsibility and good citizenship, religious duties to the community and nation (charity: tzedakah, zakat, tithes and offerings, IR sharing and care of orphans (Zunde raMambo/Isiphala seNkosi)), religious organisations' welfare work (orphanages, homes for the elderly, feeding schemes, disaster relief), volunteering, and the duty to obey just laws, pay taxes and protect public property.

concepts.name: Conflict: meaning, types and causes
concepts.description: Meaning of conflict, types (intrapersonal, interpersonal, family, community, religious, ethnic, political, international), causes (resources, power, beliefs and values, misunderstanding, injustice, inheritance disputes), effects, and conflict as both destructive and an opportunity for change. Religious conflict in particular is frs.conflict.religion-cause.

concepts.name: Religious teachings on peace and conflict
concepts.description: Peace in religions (shalom, salaam, rugare/ukuthula), IR teaching (Unhu, the role of elders), Judaism (Isaiah 2:4; Micah 4:3), Christianity (Matthew 5:9, 38-48; forgiveness, Matthew 18:21-22; just war and pacifism in outline), Islam (Islam linked with peace; reconciliation (sulh), Qur'an 49:9-10 paraphrased; lesser jihad under strict conditions), and how these teachings guide believers today.

concepts.name: Methods of managing and resolving conflict
concepts.description: Conflict management and resolution methods (dialogue, negotiation, mediation, arbitration, reconciliation, forgiveness), traditional methods (the dare/inkundla and chiefs' courts, elders and aunts and uncles as mediators, compensation and cleansing rituals such as for ngozi in outline), religious institutions as peacemakers (church, mosque and interfaith councils), and the courts and the Constitution in outline; skills for resolving conflict at school and home.

concepts.name: Religion as a source of conflict and of peace-building
concepts.description: How religion can contribute to conflict (intolerance, fundamentalism and extremism, competition for converts, disputes within religious groups, misuse of scripture, religious persecution) with factual historical and contemporary examples stated in outline only where well established (e.g. the Crusades, the Northern Ireland Troubles), and how religions build peace (interfaith dialogue, the Zimbabwe Heads of Christian Denominations, interfaith councils, mediation). No ranking of religions; no group stereotyped.
